name: Syndromic Optic Nerve Hypoplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Syndromic Optic Nerve Hypoplasia

criteria.description: Presence of unilateral or bilateral optic nerve hypoplasia confirmed by ophthalmologic examination and imaging
Identification of midline brain abnormalities such as septo-optic dysplasia or corpus callosum hypoplasia on MRI
Evidence of pituitary hormone deficiencies including growth hormone, thyroid-stimulating hormone, or adrenocorticotropic hormone
Presence of global developmental delay or intellectual disability
Clinical or imaging evidence of hypothalamic dysfunction such as temperature instability or feeding difficulties

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of optic nerve hypoplasia plus at least one midline brain anomaly
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Endocrine dysfunction and developmental delay support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Confirmed by fundoscopic exam and imaging

common.symptomName: Visual impairment ranging from mild to severe
searchTerms: vision loss from mild to severe

common.notes: Including growth hormone and thyroid hormone deficiencies
searchTerms: problems with hormone production from pituitary

common.notes: May cause temperature instability or feeding difficulties

rare.notes: Mild facial anomalies in some cases

laboratory: Hormonal assays showing pituitary hormone deficiencies (GH, TSH, ACTH)
imaging: Midline brain abnormalities including absent septum pellucidum and corpus callosum hypoplasia
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; some cases associated with HESX1 mutations
other: Ophthalmologic fundus examination revealing small optic discs
Visual evoked potentials showing reduced amplitude

distinguishingFeatures: Septo-optic dysplasia may overlap but requires absence of optic nerve hypoplasia in some cases
Coloboma presents with excavation or defect in optic nerve head rather than hypoplasia

redFlags: Signs of pituitary hormone deficiency such as hypoglycemia or growth failure
Neurological signs suggestive of midline brain malformations
references: Johns Hopkins Medicine. Optic Nerve Hypoplasia. 2023.
Orphanet Report Series: Syndromic Optic Nerve Hypoplasia. 2022.
Manning MA, et al. Optic nerve hypoplasia: clinical features and associated endocrinopathies. J Pediatr Ophthalmol Strabismus. 2021.
